problem:
$$
F(x)={\begin{aligned}0, & x\in [-\pi ,0] \\ 1, & x\in (0,\pi )\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the function $F(x)$ shown above. The Fourier series of the $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is given by

$$
f(x)∼\frac{1}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{2}{\pi (2n-1)}\operatorname{sin}⁡((2n-1)x).
$$

Select the correct options in the reasoning below.At $x=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we have

$$

$$

Since $f(x)$ is

at $x=\frac{\pi }{2},$ the corresponding Fourier series converges to

f(\frac{\pi }{2})={{field-3}}.
$$

worked_solution:
First, we rewrite our Fourier series as

$$
f(x)∼\frac{1}{2}+\frac{2}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2n-1}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡((2n-1)x).
$$

Now, notice that at $x=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡((2n-1)\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})=\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi )=(-1)^{n+1}.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is $\text{continuous}$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{2},$ the corresponding Fourier series converges to 

$$
f(\frac{\pi }{2})=1.
$$

 

Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\frac{1}{2}+\frac{2}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2n-1}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡((2n-1)\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}) \\ 1 & =\frac{1}{2}+\frac{2}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2n-1}\cdot (-1)^{n+1} \\ \frac{1}{2} & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{2n-1} \\ {\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{2n-1} & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
